latestRelease.notes:
## [0.11.0](https://github.com/grafana/loki/compare/operator/v0.10.2...operator/v0.11.0) (2026-08-18)


### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* Remove support for experimental LogQL variants() queries ([#23823](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/23823))

### Features

* **operator:** Enable multi-variant queries ([#21009](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/21009)) ([709e318](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/709e3184fc7966bc6b8eb8ca661b6b080c1c6e17))
* **operator:** Support private VPC S3 endpoints in endpoint validation ([#22395](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/22395)) ([394caef](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/394caeff2f6c8e55dca4be01bc960ac287fbfcb9))
* **operator:** Watch object storage Services for NetworkPolicy updates and surface ports in status ([#22436](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/22436)) ([12822d5](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/12822d51087550f56feca44a0f9f1ae4807c2c7e))
* Remove support for experimental LogQL variants() queries ([#23823](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/23823)) ([132e5f9](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/132e5f9cce287101a4b813564f1d6b79484b9f02))


### Bug Fixes

* **operator:** Move telemetry recording rules to OpenShift bundle ([#22814](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/22814)) ([4632368](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/4632368c7e4677191d70543cf41a8571d6eb67e3))
* **operator:** Release leader lease on shutdown so upgrades are faster ([#24042](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/24042)) ([ee0d59d](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/ee0d59d92d92a1939593e41ddd6aa704b49b592c))
* **operator:** Use ruler remote_write clients key instead of deprecated client ([#23455](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/23455)) ([f5ddb02](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/f5ddb02f41478900198178fdb25e67a095a726b9))
* **security/UNKNOWN/operator:** Update module github.com/klauspost/compress to v1.18.7 [SECURITY] (main) ([#23608](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/23608)) ([e1e4e0e](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/e1e4e0e4cad5c3e8a0fa40246a1fdfd6988d3fd6))
* **security/UNKNOWN/operator:** Update module golang.org/x/net to v0.56.0 [SECURITY] (main) ([#23388](https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/23388)) ([9362a5e](https://github.com/grafana/loki/commit/9362a5ebdc5cbbc6dc74ef45bda15ca1fa226556))

signals.title: Replace `go.uber.go/atomic` with Go standard library `sync/atomic`
signals.text: ## Summary We currently have a linter rule that blocks usage of `sync/atomic` and forces us to use `go.uber.go/atomic` instead. This rule was originally added because `sync/atomic` required atomic operations on primitive types, which was considered error-prone. However, since **Go 1.19**, the standard library `sync/atomic` package now includes typed wrappers (e.g., `atomic.Uint32`, `atomic.Int64`, `atomic.Bool`, etc.) that provide the same safety guarantees as `go.uber.go/atomic`. This makes the uber package redundant. ## Context Prometheus is also making this transition: - Issue: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14866 - PR: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18009 ## Proposed Changes 1. **Remove the linter rule** that blocks `sync/atomic` 2. **Migrate all `go.uber.go/atomic` usage** to the standard library `sync/atomic` typed wrappers 3. **Configure a linter rule** to block the old-style atomic functions that operate on primitive types (e.g., `atomic.AddInt64`, `atomic.LoadUint32`) to ensure we only use the new typed wrappers and avoid accidental misuse This approach gives us: - Fewer external dependencies - Alignment with the broader Go ecosystem - Same safety guarantees we had with uber/atomic ## References - Go 1.19 release notes on atomic types: https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.19#atomic_types - `sync/atomic` package docs: https://pkg.go.dev/sync/atomic
signals.author: Segflow

signals.title: [helm] Zone-aware ingester StatefulSets emit a duplicate `name` label and become invalid when `ingester.podLabels.name` is set
signals.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** When `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`, the three zone StatefulSet templates use the pod label `name: <prefix>ingester-zone-{a,b,c}` as the zone discriminator, and reference it from `spec.selector.matchLabels`. The same templates also append `.Values.loki.podLabels` and `.Values.ingester.podLabels` verbatim via `toYaml`, *after* their own labels and without merging. If a user sets `podLabels.name`, the rendered `spec.template.metadata.labels` therefore contains the key `name` **twice**. Two consequences: 1. The chart emits a YAML mapping with a duplicate key, which is invalid per the YAML spec regardless of what the user supplied. 2. Duplicate keys resolve last-wins, so the effective pod label becomes the user's value while `spec.selector.matchLabels` still requires the chart's. The API server rejects the StatefulSet with `` `selector` does not match template `labels` ``. The same key is also used by the per-zone headless Services (`service-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}-headless.yaml`), so a naive workaround of dropping the chart's label would leave those Services with no endpoints and break stable pod DNS. The non-zone-aware template is not affected: its selector is only `loki.ingesterSelectorLabels` and does not include `name`, so overriding `podLabels.name` there is harmless. The inconsistency looks unintentional — the zone templates added `name` to the selector without protecting it from the override path the chart itself exposes. `rollout-group` and the `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are exposed to the same collision. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0 (Loki 3.3.2). 2. Render the zone-a ingester StatefulSet with `podLabels.name` set: ```yaml # values.yaml deploymentMode: Distributed loki: storage: type: s3 bucketNames: chunks: chunks ruler: ruler admin: admin schemaConfig: configs: - from: "2024-04-01" store: tsdb object_store: s3 schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ingester: replicas: 3 podLabels: name: my-ingester # any value collides zoneAwareReplication: enabled: true read: replicas: 0 write: replicas: 0 backend: replicas: 0 ``` ``` helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.25.0 -f values.yaml \ -s templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-a.yaml ``` 3. Apply the rendered manifest to a cluster. **Expected behavior** The chart should never emit a mapping with a duplicate key, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` should always be a subset of `spec.template.metadata.labels` for any user-supplied `podLabels`. Either the chart's structurally significant labels should win over user-supplied `podLabels`, or the chart should reject the conflicting configuration with a clear message. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes 1.34 (EKS), also reproducible with `helm template` alone - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0, Loki 3.3.2) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Rendered output, `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true` — note `name` appears twice in `template.metadata.labels`, and the selector requires the first value: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a # <-- selector requires this rollout-group: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: ingester-zone-a # <-- chart's label rollout-group: ingester name: my-ingester # <-- duplicate key, wins ``` The per-zone headless Service selects on the same key: ```yaml # service-ingester-zone-a-headless.yaml selector: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a rollout-group: ingester ``` Same values with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=false` — single `name`, and the selector does not reference it, so nothing breaks: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: my-ingester ``` `kubectl apply` of the zone-aware manifest fails with: ``` The StatefulSet "loki-ingester-zone-a" is invalid: spec.template.metadata.labels: Invalid value: map[string]string{"app.kubernetes.io/component":"ingester", "app.kubernetes.io/instance":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/name":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/part-of":"memberlist", "name":"my-ingester", "rollout-group":"ingester"}: `selector` does not match template `labels` ``` --- ## Proposed fix `spec.selector` is immutable on a StatefulSet, so changing the discriminator to a dedicated key (e.g. `zone: zone-a`) would force existing zone-aware deployments to recreate their ingester StatefulSets. The options below keep the selector as it is. **Option 1 — merge the label sets so each key is emitted once (preferred).** In `templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}.yaml`, replace the `labels:` block under `spec.template.metadata` with a single merged dict, chart labels taking precedence (sprig `merge` gives precedence to the destination): ```gotemplate labels: {{- $zoneLabels := dict "app.kubernetes.io/part-of" "memberlist" "name" (printf "%singester-zone-a" (include "loki.prefixIngesterName" .)) "rollout-group" (printf "%singester" (include "loki.prefixRolloutGroup" .)) }} {{- $userLabels := merge (deepCopy (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict)) (.Values.loki.podLabels | default dict) }} {{- toYaml (merge $zoneLabels $userLabels (fromYaml (include "loki.ingesterSelectorLabels" .))) | nindent 8 }} ``` This emits every key once and guarantees `selector ⊆ labels` for any `podLabels`. Users keep the ability to add their own labels; they simply cannot silently break the selector. **Option 2 — minimal reordering.** Move the two `podLabels` blocks *above* the chart's `name` and `rollout-group` lines, so the chart's values are emitted last and win. This fixes the selector mismatch with a three-line diff, but still emits a duplicate key, so it only addresses the second consequence. **Option 3 — fail fast (complementary to either of the above).** Reject the conflicting configuration explicitly rather than rendering something that the API server will refuse: ```gotemplate {{- if and .Values.ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled (hasKey (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict) "name") }} {{- fail "ingester.podLabels may not set 'name' when ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled is true: that label is the zone discriminator used by the StatefulSet selector and the per-zone headless Services" }} {{- end }} ``` Whichever option is taken, documenting `name`, `rollout-group` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` as reserved keys under `ingester.podLabels` in `values.yaml` would help. **Workaround for anyone hitting this now** Do not set `ingester.podLabels.name` with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`. If the label is required (for example a metrics pipeline that relabels from the pod label `name`), the selector and the three per-zone headless Services have to be post-processed consistently onto a different discriminator key — all four objects must agree, or the Services lose their endpoints and stable pod DNS breaks.

signals.title: Metric queries and log queries cover different time ranges for the same request
signals.text: Log queries and histogram queries with `count_over_time` produce two different windows for the same time range and the counts don't always match. ### Steps to reproduce In our dev env, window `09:51:56.691Z` -> `09:51:57.557Z` (866ms): ``` log query {service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" -> 113 lines metric sum(count_over_time({service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" [100ms])) step=100ms -> buckets at .600 .700 .800 .900 .000 .100 .200 .300 .400 .500 -> sum = 138 ``` I pulled every line in the area and checked by hand. Of those 138, **27 fall before the window start** and **2 lines inside the window are missing** because there's no bucket for them. ### Why Two things stack up. Step alignment rounds both start and end *down* to a step multiple (`queryrangebase/step_align.go:20-23`). So `.691` becomes `.600` and `.557` becomes `.500`. That alone pulls in extra data at the front and drops data off the back. Then the first bucket counts `(t - step, t]`, so it reaches back another full step behind the already-rounded start (`logql/range_vector.go:155`, `engine/internal/executor/range_aggregation.go:41-51`). Net effect, for a request of `[start, end)`: ``` actually covered: (floor(start/step)*step - step, floor(end/step)*step] ``` Up to 2 steps of extra data at the front, up to 1 step missing at the back. Log queries don't get any of this. `engine/handler.go:180-183` skips them on purpose to preserve sub-second precision, and the log splitter doesn't align either. So the two query types genuinely answer questions about different windows. ### Impact Logs Drilldown sums the volume histogram client-side and shows it next to the log line count, with no clipping (`LogsVolumePanel.tsx:146`). Users see two numbers that should match and don't. Tracked from the UI side in grafana/logs-drilldown#2049.

signals.title: feat(kafka): support configurable SASL mechanism (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512)
signals.text: ## What this PR does / why we need it Loki's Kafka client hardcodes **SASL PLAIN** as the only authentication mechanism. Brokers configured with `sasl.enabled.mechanisms=SCRAM-SHA-256` or `SCRAM-SHA-512` only (e.g., AWS MSK, Confluent Cloud) immediately reject the handshake with `UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM`, making Loki impossible to use with those providers. This PR adds a new optional `kafka.sasl_mechanism` configuration parameter, allowing operators to choose between: - `PLAIN` (default, backward-compatible) - `SCRAM-SHA-256` - `SCRAM-SHA-512` ## Which issue(s) this PR fixes Fixes #21712 ## Changes ### Core Implementation - Added `SASLMechanism` field and validation constants to `pkg/kafka/config.go` - Updated `commonKafkaClientOptions` in `pkg/kafka/client/writer_client.go` to conditionally apply the configured SASL mechanism via switch statement - Vendored `github.com/twmb/franz-go/pkg/sasl/scram` sub-package (v1.20.7, already an indirect dependency) ### Tests (TDD approach) - Added `TestSASLMechanismValidation` in `pkg/kafka/config_test.go` to validate allowed mechanisms and reject invalid ones - Added `TestNewReaderClientSCRAMAuthentication` in `pkg/kafka/client/reader_client_test.go` with SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 subtests - Added `TestNewWriterClientSCRAMAuthentication` in `pkg/kafka/client/writer_client_test.go` with SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 subtests - Refactored existing reader/writer client tests to use explicit `SASLMechanism` field for clarity ### Documentation - Updated config reference in `docs/sources/shared/configuration.md` with the new `sasl_mechanism` parameter - Added upgrade note in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` explaining the new parameter, default behavior, and use cases - Added troubleshooting guidance in `docs/sources/operations/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-operations.md` for `UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM` errors ### Text Consistency - Updated flag help text in `pkg/kafka/config.go` to remove outdated "PLAIN-only" wording - Updated generated docs to match the new, mechanism-agnostic descriptions ## Special notes for your reviewer 1. **Backward Compatibility**: The default value is `PLAIN`, preserving full backward compatibility. No action is required for existing deployments. 2. **Testing**: All tests follow table-driven patterns with explicit mechanism values. SCRAM tests create fresh clusters per mechanism to isolate setup. 3. **Vendor**: The `scram` sub-package was already available transitively; only needed to copy it into vendor and update `modules.txt`. 4. **TDD**: Implementation follows TDD: failing tests → production code → all tests pass. ## Checklist - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide - [x] Documentation added (config reference, upgrade guide, troubleshooting) - [x] Tests updated (config validation + reader/writer SCRAM authentication) - [x] Title follows conventional commits format: `feat(kafka): ...` - [x] Upgrade guide updated: `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [x] No deprecated/deleted config changes required <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches Kafka authentication and client initialization; while default remains `PLAIN`, misconfiguration or vendor/mechanism selection issues could prevent Loki components from connecting to Kafka at startup. > > **Overview** > Adds a new Kafka config/flag `sasl_mechanism` to select SASL auth (`PLAIN` default, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512`), including validation that rejects unsupported values. > > Updates Kafka client option wiring to negotiate SCRAM when selected (in `commonKafkaClientOptions`), and extends tests to cover SCRAM end-to-end for reader/writer clients and the partition `ReaderService`. > > Documentation is updated with the new parameter, an upgrade note, and troubleshooting guidance for `UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM`; the franz-go SCRAM SASL implementation is vendored and `vendor/modules.txt` updated accordingly. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 345367966f93875e7afc080aa03de3615a325eb6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(storage): Pre-compute SHA-256 to avoid aws-chunked on PutObject
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: When `ChecksumAlgorithm` is set on `PutObjectInput` without a pre-computed value, the AWS SDK v2 switches to trailing-checksum mode which wraps the body in `aws-chunked` transfer encoding. OpenStack Swift and other S3-compatible backends reject this with `501 NotImplemented`. This PR pre-computes the SHA-256 hash upfront and passes it as `ChecksumSHA256`. This causes the SDK checksum middleware to detect that the header is already present and skip the `aws-chunked` trailing-checksum path entirely. This cleanly satisfies Object Lock requirements (which require the checksum header) while remaining compatible with S3-compatible backends (which don't support `aws-chunked`). **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #21791 **Special notes for your reviewer**: I've added two regression tests to `s3_storage_client_test.go`: 1. `TestPutObject_NoAWSChunkedEncoding`: Verifies that `PutObject` sends the `x-amz-checksum-sha256` as a plain header and does NOT use `Content-Encoding: aws-chunked`. 2. `TestPutObject_SwiftRejects_AWSChunked`: A mock server that behaves like OpenStack Swift (returns `501 NotImplemented` when it sees `aws-chunked`). It proves that the fix makes the request pass successfully against a Swift-like API. Because `clientutil.ReadSeeker` already guarantees the body is fully buffered in memory (`bytes.Reader`), the SHA-256 pre-computation reads from RAM and adds zero extra I/O. **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. [Example PR](https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/10840/commits/0d4416a4b03739583349934b96f272fb4f685d15)

signals.title: fix: Recognise thanos/minio S3 throttling errors as retryable
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: S3 throttling responses (`SlowDown`, `503`, `429`) were not being treated as retryable when the object client runs on the thanos/objstore backend (`use_thanos_objstore: true`), which is the default for our object stores. `IsStorageThrottledErr` only matched the AWS SDK's `smithy.APIError`, but the thanos S3 client is backed by minio-go, which returns `minio.ErrorResponse`. As a result, on throttling: - congestion control classified the error as non-retryable, - so it never retried, and its AIMD controller never backed off, and - every throttle surfaced immediately as a `failed downloading chunks` error. This PR makes `IsStorageThrottledErr` also recognise `minio.ErrorResponse` throttling/5xx codes (with an HTTP-status fallback for 429 / any 5xx), so both the legacy AWS-SDK client and the thanos/minio client share one retryability definition. Retries and AIMD back-off now engage as designed, absorbing transient throttles instead of failing the chunk fetch. **Special notes for your reviewer**: - The fix lives in `IsStorageThrottledErr`, which is the single retryability entry point used by *both* the legacy S3 client and the thanos `ObjectClientAdapter` (`storeType == s3` → `aws.IsRetryableErr`), so both paths benefit, and there's no duplicated code-list. - `errors.As` is used so wrapped errors (thanos wraps with `pkg/errors`) are still matched. - Tests, in increasing scope: - unit: `TestIsRetryableErr` — minio `SlowDown`/`ServiceUnavailable`/`InternalError`/`TooManyRequests`, wrapped errors, status-only fallback, and negatives (`NoSuchKey`, `AccessDenied`). - wiring: `TestObjectClientAdapter_IsRetryableErr_S3Minio` — locks `storeType == s3` → minio-aware retryability. - end-to-end: `TestCongestionControl_S3Throttling_*` — drive the real AIMD controller → LimitedRetrier → thanos adapter → minio-go → fake S3 returning `503 SlowDown`, asserting retries fire, AIMD backs off, `non_retryable_errors == 0`, and a transient throttle is absorbed. - No config or API changes; behaviour only changes for previously misclassified throttling errors. **Checklist** - [ ] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory.

signals.title: fix(compactor): Delete chunks marked for deletion when compactor leadership changes
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: Retention and delete requests are applied in two phases. The compaction removes the chunk references from the index and records them in a marker file; a sweeper then deletes those chunks from the object store once `retention_delete_delay` (2 hours by default) has elapsed. Marker files are written to the local disk of whichever instance currently wins the compactor ring leader election, and only the elected instance runs the sweeper (`tablesManager.start` is called only from the leader branch of `Compactor.loop`). In SSD mode the leadership can move to another instance inside the delay window, and markers on local disk are not visible to the other instances, so the chunks they reference are never deleted from the object store. As @slim-bean notes in #11119, this is not only wasted object storage. Chunks marked because of a delete request are dropped from the index but never removed from storage, so a delete request submitted through the delete API silently fails to delete the data even though the API reported success — which matters for anyone relying on the API to satisfy a data deletion obligation. @Perdjesk's comment on the issue reports the same failure mode reachable from the default Helm SSD values. While digging into this I also found a second, sharper failure: the marker processor cannot be restarted. `newMarkerReader` creates one context per processor and `Stop` cancels it, so once an instance has lost the leader election a later `Start` returns immediately (`r.ctx.Err() != nil`) and that instance never sweeps again for the rest of the process lifetime — not even while it is the elected leader. This makes the "unless that node becomes the leader elected compactor again" escape hatch mentioned in the issue ineffective, and it fits @duj4's observation on the issue of a compactor service starting again after a stop. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #11119 **Solution and trade-offs**: The issue lists two solutions: 1. marker files should go to object storage 2. all compactors could run sweepers to make sure they cleanup any marker files they have even if they aren't the elected leader Option 1 already landed in #19689: `-compactor.deletion-marker-object-store-prefix` stores markers under an object storage prefix, and existing local markers are copied over on startup. It is opt-in and empty by default, so the default configuration — including the default Helm SSD values, where `backend` runs the compactor with 3 replicas — is still affected. This PR implements option 2 for that default. Each instance now runs the chunk sweeper for the markers on its own disk regardless of whether it currently owns the compaction, so a former leader finishes deleting the chunks it marked. Deliberately, this applies only when markers are on local disk. When `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix` is set the markers live in one shared prefix that every instance can already see, so sweeping continues to run on the elected instance only. Sweeping a shared prefix from every instance would duplicate the object storage deletes and let two instances race over the same marker file, whereas local markers are private to their instance by construction, so there is no contention. I did not change the default of `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix`. Flipping it would change the storage layout and the object storage request profile of every existing deployment, which seems like a maintainer call rather than something to slip into a bug fix. Happy to follow up separately if you would like that instead. `retention_delete_delay` semantics are unchanged: eligibility is still decided by `markerProcessor.availableFiles` from the marker file timestamp, so the window that lets index gateways refresh their index copies before chunks disappear is preserved. The sweep just happens on the instance holding the marker instead of nowhere. **Backwards compatibility / upgrade**: * No configuration change, no new option, no default value change. * Marker file format and on-disk layout are untouched, so a downgrade is safe: markers written before or after this change are read identically by either version. * Markers already sitting on the local disk of a former leader when the new version starts are picked up on startup. That backlog is exactly what the fix drains, so no migration step is needed. The pre-existing `retention.CopyMarkers` migration from the legacy `retention/markers` and `retention/<store>/markers` directories into the period-specific directories is left as is. * Deployments already using `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix` keep their current behaviour, minus the restart bug. * No upgrade guide entry, since no operator action is required. Happy to add one if you would rather call the behaviour change out explicitly. * One consequence worth flagging: instances that are not the leader now emit the existing `no marks file found` sweeper log line once a minute per period. It is a local directory listing, so the cost is negligible, but the line was previously logged only by the leader. Let me know if you would prefer it downgraded to debug. **Special notes for your reviewer**: Two tests, both verified to fail before the change: * `Test_markerProcessor_Restart` — processes a mark, stops the processor the way a lost leader election does, writes another mark and starts it again. Before the fix the second mark is never processed (`Condition never satisfied`). * `TestCompactor_SweepsOwnMarkersWithoutLeadership` — writes a chunk and a marker for it, then runs `Compactor.loop` with a ring that never elects this instance, and asserts the chunk is removed from the object store. Before the fix the chunk survives (`chunk marked for deletion was not swept`). Verification: `go test ./pkg/compactor/... -count=1` passes, as does `-race` on `./pkg/compactor/ ./pkg/compactor/retention/`; `go build ./cmd/loki` and `gofmt` are clean. The docs change mentions `-compactor.deletion-marker-object-store-prefix` on the retention page next to the existing persistent-disk recommendation, since that option was not referenced there at all. **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [x] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [x] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` — n/a, no operator action required - [x] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory — n/a

signals.title: feat(storage): Add OCI Thanos object store backend
signals.text: ## Problem Loki does not currently expose OCI Object Storage as a supported Thanos object-store backend. OCI users therefore have to use the S3-compatible API and static Customer Secret Keys. This prevents using OCI-native authentication mechanisms such as: - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal ## Proposed solution Add `oci` to Loki's Thanos object-store backends by reusing the OCI provider from Thanos objstore. Proposed configuration: ``` storage_config: use_thanos_objstore: true object_store: oci: provider: instance-principal bucket: loki-data region: ap-tokyo-1 max_request_retries: 3 request_retry_interval: 1 schema_config: configs: - from: 2026-08-01 store: tsdb object_store: oci schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ``` ## Security benefit No OCI Customer Secret Key needs to be stored in Loki configuration or Kubernetes Secrets. ## Scope - Loki TSDB object storage - Instance Principal - Unit tests - OCI/OKE integration test documentation Named stores and Helm chart support can be submitted separately. ## Validation A standalone Thanos OCI client has already been validated successfully against OCI Object Storage from OKE using Instance Principal. Fixes #23687

signals.title: feat(logql): Add approx_count_distinct aggregation
signals.text: ## Summary - Adds experimental LogQL `approx_count_distinct` to approximate distinct values of a label or extracted field without creating one series per distinct value. - Instant queries only; each output group holds one HyperLogLog sketch (precision 14, ~16 KiB dense, ~0.81% nominal RSE). - Supports index sharding when `approx_count_distinct` is listed in `shard_aggregations`; shards return mergeable sketches and the frontend merges before estimating. - Requires `frontend.encoding: protobuf` (JSON internal transport is rejected). Result caching is disabled for these queries. ### Syntax ```logql approx_count_distinct( <counted field>, <log expression> [<duration>] ) by (<grouping fields>) ``` Example: ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` `by (...)` is required. `unwrap`, ungrouped forms, `without`, and prefix grouping are not supported. The counted field must not appear in `by (...)`. ### Enablement ```yaml limits_config: shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct] frontend: encoding: protobuf ``` Off by default until `approx_count_distinct` is added to `shard_aggregations`. Grafana Cloud can follow the existing `approx_topk` enablement pattern in `ksonnet/lib/loki-cloud-mixin/limits.libsonnet`. ### Implementation notes - Public AST: `LabelAggregationExpr`; shard children use internal `CountDistinctSketchExpr` (merge-before-estimate). - Distinct-value extractor hashes the raw string with xxhash64 into `Sample.Value` via `Float64frombits`; evaluator inserts with `InsertHash`. - Range splitting is rejected as unsafe for HLL estimates; outer non-HLL aggregations over this op remain non-shardable. - Output cardinality is bounded by grouping labels / `max_query_series`, not by distinct counted values. Peak sketch memory scales with group count (~16 KiB dense per group) and is not capped by `max_query_series` alone. ## Test plan - [ ] `go test ./pkg/logql/ ./pkg/logql/syntax/ ./pkg/logql/log/ ./pkg/querier/queryrange/ ./pkg/logproto/ ./pkg/chunkenc/` - [ ] Instant query returns per-group estimates; missing/empty counted fields are skipped - [ ] With `shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct]`, shard mapper rewrites to merge-before-estimate and merged estimates match local evaluation - [ ] Without the gate / without protobuf encoding, queries are rejected - [ ] Range queries are rejected - [ ] Staging enablement before broader rollout

signals.title: docs: Note that index/stats and index/volume are not deletion-aware
signals.text: Documents the caveat reported in #23807. `SelectLogs` and `SelectSamples` pass the filters from pending and recently processed delete requests into the query via `deletion.DeletesForUserQuery` (`pkg/querier/querier.go`), so log and metric queries are exact as soon as a delete request is processed. `IndexStats` and `Volume` in the same file take no delete parameters — they report what the index holds, so the same stream selector can keep reporting deleted data until the compactor has rewritten the index and the pre-rewrite index files have aged out. `Volume` also fans out to the ingesters, whose not-yet-flushed chunks are counted before any delete filtering applies to them, while `IndexStats` is store-only. The reference already carries a caveats list for `index/stats`; this adds the deletion caveat there and an equivalent note on `index/volume` / `index/volume_range`, which had none. It also points at `bytes_over_time` for accounting that has to be exact, since that path is deletion-aware. This is documentation only. The reporter's second ask — making these endpoints deletion-aware, or deduplicating chunk identity across the merged compactor-rewritten and ingester-uploaded index views — is a behaviour change I did not want to guess at, so I have left it to #23807. Verified against `main`: the delete-parameter asymmetry between `SelectLogs`/`SelectSamples` and `IndexStats`/`Volume` is still present, and `Volume` still queries the ingesters.

signals.title: chore: Log usage of failed queries with failure cause
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: The query-frontend only logs query usage stats (the `metrics.go` line) for queries that execute successfully. Expensive queries that fail leave no usage record, making them invisible to usage analysis. This PR makes the query-frontend emit a dedicated log line for failed log and metric queries, reporting the number of bytes the query processed before failing and a classified, actionable cause of the failure. Implementation notes: - **The existing stats line is untouched.** The new line is emitted from the stats-collector middleware, not from `pkg/logql/metrics.go` (zero changes to that file). The successful-query stats line keeps its exact shape, is never emitted for a failed query, and failed-query usage does not feed into any of the existing usage metrics, latency histograms, or analytics. A new counter `loki_logql_querystats_failed_query_usage_recorded_total{category}` tracks the number of emitted lines. - **Scope is log/metric queries only** — the only query types whose responses carry querier-filled statistics; any other type could only ever report zeroes. - **Partial usage accumulation**: a new `stats.PartialContext` lives under its own context key so the nested stats contexts opened by the engine and the sharding middleware don't shadow it. The split and shard fan-out error paths join the stats of already-completed sub-queries into it. Sibling cancellations propagate the causal error (`context.Cause`), so a real failure isn't misreported as a client cancellation. - **Failure classification**: `server.ClassifyFailure(err)` maps an error to a bounded `failure_category` and a fine-grained `failure_reason`, reusing the canonical `ClientHTTPStatusAndError` so the logged status matches what the client is served. All configured limits classify as `failure_category=limit`. - **Sentinel-based classification for in-process errors**: byte-limit, query-length, max-entries, and parallelism rejections raised in the frontend wrap a sentinel (`errors.Is`) around the unchanged client-facing httpgrpc error. `querySizeLimiter` now carries an explicit `{limit name, sentinel, template}` spec instead of reverse-mapping its message template (`guessLimitName` is gone). Message-prefix matching remains only as documented defense-in-depth for the same limits raised on queriers or the v2 engine, where error identity cannot survive httpgrpc serialization. - `stats.Context`'s snapshot accessors now take the context mutex so snapshots no longer tear against `JoinResults`/`MergeIndex`; the failed-query path additionally avoids the residual atomic-counter race by only ever reading the `PartialContext`. - Successful shards/patterns queries no longer log a spurious "failed to record query metrics" error in the frontend. **Special notes for your reviewer**: - Client-facing error messages and status codes are unchanged throughout: the sentinel wrapping uses `%w`, and response construction extracts the embedded `httpgrpc.HTTPResponse` via `errors.As`, so the sentinel prefix never reaches the client. This invariant is pinned byte-for-byte by tests driving the real middlewares (`TestWrappedLimitErrorStatusPreserved`, plus classification assertions through `NewLimitsMiddleware`, `NewLimitedRoundTripper`, and the entries-limit tripperware). - The concurrent split fan-out path is covered by a `-race` test with live sibling writers. - The new line is emitted at info level and also covers client-cancelled queries (zero usage, `failure_category=canceled`) — expect some volume from dashboard-refresh churn; the fields make it filterable. - Failed queries that are neither split nor sharded report `total_bytes=0B` by construction: error responses carry no statistics over the wire, so only completed sibling sub-requests can contribute.

signals.title: fix: Add meaningful chunk fetch loss metrics
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: `Fetcher.FetchChunks` logs an object store error and then returns a nil error. The query gets fewer log lines, HTTP 200, and no signal. We do not measure how often this occurs yet. This PR adds `loki_chunk_fetcher_failures_total{source,reason}`. It counts each lost chunk and the reason for the loss. This PR yet doesn't change the end-user behavior yet. It only addresses the propagation of metrics downstream. Also, a cache decode failure no longer reports `msg="failed downloading chunks"`, because that call never used storage. Currently, the counter over-reports. Query iterators fetch one batch ahead and do not join that batch on close, so a query that stops early still counts that batch. Most of that is `reason=canceled`. Use `reason!~"canceled|deadline"` for the data loss signal. Subsequent PRs to extend these will follow. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #<issue number> **Special notes for your reviewer**: **Checklist** - [ ] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [ ] Tests updated - [ ] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. signals.title: feat(indexgateway): Add admission control to bound concurrent requests
signals.text: ## Summary The index gateway currently has no bound on concurrent request execution. This PR ports the admission-control pattern used in Mimir's store-gateway (same dskit building blocks): at most N requests execute at once; excess requests wait for a free slot; requests that wait longer than the configured timeout are rejected with HTTP 503. This feature is **experimental** and **disabled by default** (`-index-gateway.max-concurrent=0`). ## Error handling choice Load-shed rejections now use `httpgrpc.Error(503, ...)`, matching distributor convention (`pkg/distributor/distributor.go`). This gives us the behavior we want without broad shared-mapping changes: - No `pkg/util/server/error.go` mapping changes required. - 503 survives wrapped errors (important for `GetShards`, which wraps RPC errors). - Unrelated transport-level gRPC `Unavailable` failures are not implicitly remapped. ## Test updates Time-dependent gate tests now run under `testing/synctest`, which removes wall-clock sleeps/timeouts and makes the cancellation ordering deterministic. ## Follow-up When all replicas are saturated, retrying across replicas can amplify pressure by serially spending queue timeout at each target. Follow-up issue: https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/24051 ## Dev validation note Cloud dev-environment validation is planned next using an in-progress harness; this PR does not include local docker-compose evidence.

signals.text: One of the biggest costs when reading postings is opening and closing files. This change pools file handles, reducing that cost significantly. signals.title: chore: Read series records through one scan per postings pass
signals.text: The stream reader built a fresh decbuf for every series record: a pooled file handle, a 4 KiB bufio buffer, a seek to the record, and a read. A series ref is the record's file offset divided by 16 and postings hand out refs in ascending order, so consecutive series in a result set are usually adjacent in the file and often inside the same 4 KiB window. The read-ahead that would have covered a series' neighbours was discarded by the next ResetAt before it could be used. Hold one decbuf for the whole postings pass instead, moving forward by discarding buffered bytes when the next record is within the buffer and repositioning otherwise. Nothing depends on refs being ascending: an out-of-order ref just repositions, which costs what it costs today. This PR changes the Reader interface to support this streaming approach. signals.title: fix(indexgateway): Cap client-side in-flight requests to avoid retry amplification
signals.text: Fixes #24051 ## What this does `poolDo` had no bound on concurrent in-flight requests to the index gateway pool. With `maxRetries = -1` (used by 6 of the 7 call sites), a client under load would serially walk every address in the pool on failure, each attempt bounded by that gateway's own admission-control queue timeout (from #23932). When every replica is shedding load, this amplifies load at exactly the moment the pool is most overloaded, instead of failing fast. ## The fix Adds a configurable client-side cap on in-flight requests (`-index-gateway-client.max-in-flight-requests`, default 2048, 0 = unlimited to match the convention used elsewhere in this file). The check runs at the very start of `poolDo`, before any tenant lookup or address resolution — once at capacity, requests are rejected immediately with a distinct error instead of retrying across the whole pool. Tracked via a new `loki_index_gateway_request_rejected_total` counter so operators can see this happening rather than it being silent. One deliberate tradeoff: the cap check is check-then-act, not a single atomic compare-and-swap, so under concurrency the actual in-flight count can briefly exceed the configured cap by a small margin. Noted in a code comment — this is acceptable for a soft limit meant to prevent amplification storms, not a hard resource cap. ## Testing Added four tests covering: rejection at cap (verified by confirming the capacity error returns before any tenant/address lookup would even be attempted), the in-flight counter decrementing after both success and failure paths (proving the `defer` fires on every exit), and `MaxInFlightRequests = 0` correctly disabling the check. Happy to adjust the default cap value or error message if you'd prefer something different.

signals.title: chore(deps): Upgrade to moby from docker (backport release-3.7.x)
signals.text: This PR backports #22034 to `release-3.7.x`. Because of drift, the cherry-pick hit a number of conflicts which had to be manually resolved. ## What it does Replaces the EOL `github.com/docker/docker` with the split-out moby modules. `docker/docker` is now gone from the branch entirely which clears a number of CVEs. ## Where it differs from the original Upstream only touched `clients/cmd/docker-driver` because `clients/pkg/promtail/targets/docker` and `pkg/framedstdcopy` had already been deleted from `main` by then. Both still live on `release-3.7.x` and both imported `docker/docker`, so they needed updating - even though they are now effectly unused. (Target for another backport PR). ## Testing All CI tests are passing but this was also verified by hand to match the old driver behavior. ## Known, but not introduced here An adversarial review turned up two issues in `clients/cmd/docker-driver` that come straight from #22034 and are already shipping on `main`: `logdriver.Decode` no longer caps frame size (the old `Uint32DelimitedReader` was built with `1e6`), and `consumeLog` no longer defers `lf.Close()`. Both are being handled on `main` separately rather than diverging this backport.
signals.author: jnewbigin

signals.title: fix(ruler): Restore remote-write secrets lost by config Clone
signals.text: ## Summary - `RemoteWriteConfig.Clone` now restores every `Secret`-typed field reachable from a remote-write client after its YAML round-trip: - `OAuth2.ClientSecret`/`ClientCertificateKey` - `Authorization.Credentials` (including a bare `bearer_token` migrated into it during that same round-trip) - `SigV4Config.SecretKey` - `AzureADConfig.OAuth.ClientSecret`/`Certificate.CertificatePassword` - `TLSConfig.Key` at both the top level and inside `OAuth2` - `HTTPClientConfig.ProxyConnectHeader` and `OAuth2`'s own copy - `HTTPHeaders.Headers[*].Secrets` - `BasicAuth.Password` (existing) - `ProxyConnectHeader` is deep-copied via a new `cloneProxyHeader` helper so when `getTenantRemoteWriteConfig` later merges per-tenant overrides with `mergo.Merge`, reassigned maps are not aliased to the shared base config and mutated - Adds `TestTenantRemoteWriteOAuth2SecretSurvivesClone`, reproducing the leak through the real `getTenantConfig` path rather than calling `Clone` directly. - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_RestoresSecrets`, which reflects over `RemoteWriteConfig`'s type graph to find every reachable `Secret` field, asserts a fixture sets a value at each one, then asserts `Clone` preserves every one of them. - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_DoesNotAliasContainers`, asserting that mutating a clone's map- or slice-typed secret containers doesn't affect the original - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_RestoresMigratedBearerToken`, covering the `bearer_token` case separately since the field its secret ends up in differs from the field it started in. `Clone` round-trips a `RemoteWriteConfig` through YAML to produce an independent per-tenant copy, but Prometheus's `config_util.Secret` type obfuscates several values to the literal string `<secret>`. Before this change `Clone` only restored `BasicAuth.Password`, so every other auth mechanism silently lost its real secret the moment a tenant's config was cloned The comprehensive test walks the type graph with reflection rather than checking a fixed field list, so a future Prometheus vendor bump that adds a new `Secret` field anywhere in this type graph fails the coverage check immediately

signals.title: feat: Collapse max request body size and decompressed size
signals.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: This commit collapses the max-recv-msg-size, which measures the size of the HTTP request body, and the max decompressed size (i.e. if the request has been Gzip or Snappy compressed) into a single flag. As far as Loki is concerned, we only care about the maximum size of the actual logproto that is parsed out of the request after any decompression. It doesn't make sense to have two different flags for this with the same value. You will notice that in http.go we pass the same flag twice to push.ParseRequest. This is temporary, and the only reason for it is to make the diff smaller and easier to review. signals.title: fix(docker-driver): Bound log frame size and restore stream cleanup
signals.text: This PR hardens the docker logging plugin's frame decoder and restores the stream cleanup it lost when the driver moved from `github.com/docker/docker` to `github.com/moby/moby/v2` in #22034. ## The problems **Unbounded allocation.** That migration replaced gogo/protobuf's `Uint32DelimitedReader`, which was constructed with a `1e6` max message size, with a local length-prefixed codec carrying no bound at all. `Decode` sized its read buffer straight off the 4-byte prefix, so a corrupt frame could ask for a 4GiB allocation and exhaust the memory. **Leaked resources.** The migration also lost `consumeLog`'s `defer lf.Close()`. If the fifo stream dies before `StopLogging` runs, the fifo, the Loki client and the json logger are all left open. **Error handling.** Error recovery cannot resynchronise a length-prefixed stream, so with a frame cap in place we don't retry but return a hard error. ## The fix - Reject frames declaring more than `1e6` bytes before sizing the buffer. The prefix is compared as a `uint32`, because `int(...)` wraps negative on a 32-bit build and would slip straight past the bound into a panicking slice expression. - Return `ErrPayloadUnmarshal` for a payload that will not unmarshal, so `consumeLog` can skip that frame and carry on. Every other decode error leaves the offset unknown and still shuts the consumer down. - Restore the deferred `logPair.Close()`, guarded with a `sync.Once` since both `consumeLog` and `StopLogging` can now reach it. ## Testing `logdriver` new tests cover round-trip encoding, an oversized prefix (just-over-limit and 4GiB), a frame at the limit, recovery after a bad payload, and that an oversized frame is *not* reported as recoverable. On the driver side there are tests for `Close` idempotency, for skipping a bad payload while still shipping the frames either side of it, and for stopping dead on a framing error.
signals.author: jnewbigin

signals.title: ci(release): Bump loki-release and publish the docker driver plugin again
signals.text: This PR gets the `loki-docker-driver` plugin shipping again on `release-3.7.x`, in two separable commits. ## `chore(ci): Bump loki-release to 6cba58c` `make update-loki-release-sha` moves the pin from `79fc5eab` to `6cba58c3b708`, ten commits on, and regenerates the workflows. The generated output barely moves: `RELEASE_LIB_REF` and the `create-github-app-token` action SHA, 23 lines each way across five files. The branch was sitting **one commit short** of what it needed. `fix(ci): Publish docker plugin to GAR via crane` (loki-release #389) landed on the same day as the pinned `79fc5eab`, just before it, so it never came across. The bump also picks up loki-release's own security updates for `klauspost/compress`, `mongo-driver` and the Go toolchain directive. ## `ci(release): Publish the docker driver plugin again` Flips `publishDockerPlugins` back to `true`, which regenerates a `publishDockerPlugins` job in `release.yml`: pull the built plugins from the GAR generic repo, start a local registry, push the plugin into it, then mirror to `PLUGIN_IMAGE_PREFIX` with crane as an OCI layout. `publishRelease` now waits on that job, so a release cannot publish without its plugins. Plugin publishing was turned off in #22549 when stable images moved to the GAR mirror, because GAR will not accept the `application/vnd.docker.plugin.v1+json` media type. The crane mirror in the bumped library is the workaround, which is why the two commits go together — the flip is inert without the bump, and would fail the same way it did before #22549 disabled it. ## Worth a reviewer's judgement **This diverges release plumbing between branches.** `main` still has `publishDockerPlugins=false`, so merging this leaves `release-3.7.x` publishing plugins and `main` not. That is the wrong direction for a maintenance branch as a rule, and the argument for doing it here is simply that 3.7 is where the plugin needs to ship. The flip is its own commit precisely so it can be dropped if you would rather `main` went first and this came back as a backport. **The bump is to loki-release main's tip, not to the crane fix specifically.** `make update-loki-release-sha` always targets the tip; pinning `0b88c65fb252` on its own would mean hand-editing the SHA and skipping the security updates. ## Testing `make release-workflows-check` passes on a clean tree, so the committed YAML matches what the jsonnet generates. The plugin publish path itself cannot be exercised outside a real release run — it needs the GAR generic repo and the release artefacts — so that first exercise will be the next 3.7 patch release.

signal.title: chore(deps): Upgrade to moby from docker (backport release-3.7.x)
signal.text: This PR backports #22034 to `release-3.7.x`. Because of drift, the cherry-pick hit a number of conflicts which had to be manually resolved. ## What it does Replaces the EOL `github.com/docker/docker` with the split-out moby modules. `docker/docker` is now gone from the branch entirely which clears a number of CVEs. ## Where it differs from the original Upstream only touched `clients/cmd/docker-driver` because `clients/pkg/promtail/targets/docker` and `pkg/framedstdcopy` had already been deleted from `main` by then. Both still live on `release-3.7.x` and both imported `docker/docker`, so they needed updating - even though they are now effectly unused. (Target for another backport PR). ## Testing All CI tests are passing but this was also verified by hand to match the old driver behavior. ## Known, but not introduced here An adversarial review turned up two issues in `clients/cmd/docker-driver` that come straight from #22034 and are already shipping on `main`: `logdriver.Decode` no longer caps frame size (the old `Uint32DelimitedReader` was built with `1e6`), and `consumeLog` no longer defers `lf.Close()`. Both are being handled on `main` separately rather than diverging this backport.

signal.title: fix(compactor): Delete chunks marked for deletion when compactor leadership changes
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: Retention and delete requests are applied in two phases. The compaction removes the chunk references from the index and records them in a marker file; a sweeper then deletes those chunks from the object store once `retention_delete_delay` (2 hours by default) has elapsed. Marker files are written to the local disk of whichever instance currently wins the compactor ring leader election, and only the elected instance runs the sweeper (`tablesManager.start` is called only from the leader branch of `Compactor.loop`). In SSD mode the leadership can move to another instance inside the delay window, and markers on local disk are not visible to the other instances, so the chunks they reference are never deleted from the object store. As @slim-bean notes in #11119, this is not only wasted object storage. Chunks marked because of a delete request are dropped from the index but never removed from storage, so a delete request submitted through the delete API silently fails to delete the data even though the API reported success — which matters for anyone relying on the API to satisfy a data deletion obligation. @Perdjesk's comment on the issue reports the same failure mode reachable from the default Helm SSD values. While digging into this I also found a second, sharper failure: the marker processor cannot be restarted. `newMarkerReader` creates one context per processor and `Stop` cancels it, so once an instance has lost the leader election a later `Start` returns immediately (`r.ctx.Err() != nil`) and that instance never sweeps again for the rest of the process lifetime — not even while it is the elected leader. This makes the "unless that node becomes the leader elected compactor again" escape hatch mentioned in the issue ineffective, and it fits @duj4's observation on the issue of a compactor service starting again after a stop. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #11119 **Solution and trade-offs**: The issue lists two solutions: 1. marker files should go to object storage 2. all compactors could run sweepers to make sure they cleanup any marker files they have even if they aren't the elected leader Option 1 already landed in #19689: `-compactor.deletion-marker-object-store-prefix` stores markers under an object storage prefix, and existing local markers are copied over on startup. It is opt-in and empty by default, so the default configuration — including the default Helm SSD values, where `backend` runs the compactor with 3 replicas — is still affected. This PR implements option 2 for that default. Each instance now runs the chunk sweeper for the markers on its own disk regardless of whether it currently owns the compaction, so a former leader finishes deleting the chunks it marked. Deliberately, this applies only when markers are on local disk. When `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix` is set the markers live in one shared prefix that every instance can already see, so sweeping continues to run on the elected instance only. Sweeping a shared prefix from every instance would duplicate the object storage deletes and let two instances race over the same marker file, whereas local markers are private to their instance by construction, so there is no contention. I did not change the default of `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix`. Flipping it would change the storage layout and the object storage request profile of every existing deployment, which seems like a maintainer call rather than something to slip into a bug fix. Happy to follow up separately if you would like that instead. `retention_delete_delay` semantics are unchanged: eligibility is still decided by `markerProcessor.availableFiles` from the marker file timestamp, so the window that lets index gateways refresh their index copies before chunks disappear is preserved. The sweep just happens on the instance holding the marker instead of nowhere. **Backwards compatibility / upgrade**: * No configuration change, no new option, no default value change. * Marker file format and on-disk layout are untouched, so a downgrade is safe: markers written before or after this change are read identically by either version. * Markers already sitting on the local disk of a former leader when the new version starts are picked up on startup. That backlog is exactly what the fix drains, so no migration step is needed. The pre-existing `retention.CopyMarkers` migration from the legacy `retention/markers` and `retention/<store>/markers` directories into the period-specific directories is left as is. * Deployments already using `deletion_marker_object_store_prefix` keep their current behaviour, minus the restart bug. * No upgrade guide entry, since no operator action is required. Happy to add one if you would rather call the behaviour change out explicitly. * One consequence worth flagging: instances that are not the leader now emit the existing `no marks file found` sweeper log line once a minute per period. It is a local directory listing, so the cost is negligible, but the line was previously logged only by the leader. Let me know if you would prefer it downgraded to debug. **Special notes for your reviewer**: Two tests, both verified to fail before the change: * `Test_markerProcessor_Restart` — processes a mark, stops the processor the way a lost leader election does, writes another mark and starts it again. Before the fix the second mark is never processed (`Condition never satisfied`). * `TestCompactor_SweepsOwnMarkersWithoutLeadership` — writes a chunk and a marker for it, then runs `Compactor.loop` with a ring that never elects this instance, and asserts the chunk is removed from the object store. Before the fix the chunk survives (`chunk marked for deletion was not swept`). Verification: `go test ./pkg/compactor/... -count=1` passes, as does `-race` on `./pkg/compactor/ ./pkg/compactor/retention/`; `go build ./cmd/loki` and `gofmt` are clean. The docs change mentions `-compactor.deletion-marker-object-store-prefix` on the retention page next to the existing persistent-disk recommendation, since that option was not referenced there at all. **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [x] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [x] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` — n/a, no operator action required - [x] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory — n/a

signal.title: feat(logql): Add approx_count_distinct aggregation
signal.text: ## Summary - Adds experimental LogQL `approx_count_distinct` to approximate distinct values of a label or extracted field without creating one series per distinct value. - Instant queries only; each output group holds one HyperLogLog sketch (precision 14, ~16 KiB dense, ~0.81% nominal RSE). - Supports index sharding when `approx_count_distinct` is listed in `shard_aggregations`; shards return mergeable sketches and the frontend merges before estimating. - Requires `frontend.encoding: protobuf` (JSON internal transport is rejected). Result caching is disabled for these queries. ### Syntax ```logql approx_count_distinct( <counted field>, <log expression> [<duration>] ) by (<grouping fields>) ``` Example: ```logql approx_count_distinct( mac_address, {job="devices"} | json [1d] ) by (version) ``` `by (...)` is required. `unwrap`, ungrouped forms, `without`, and prefix grouping are not supported. The counted field must not appear in `by (...)`. ### Enablement ```yaml limits_config: shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct] frontend: encoding: protobuf ``` Off by default until `approx_count_distinct` is added to `shard_aggregations`. Grafana Cloud can follow the existing `approx_topk` enablement pattern in `ksonnet/lib/loki-cloud-mixin/limits.libsonnet`. ### Implementation notes - Public AST: `LabelAggregationExpr`; shard children use internal `CountDistinctSketchExpr` (merge-before-estimate). - Distinct-value extractor hashes the raw string with xxhash64 into `Sample.Value` via `Float64frombits`; evaluator inserts with `InsertHash`. - Range splitting is rejected as unsafe for HLL estimates; outer non-HLL aggregations over this op remain non-shardable. - Output cardinality is bounded by grouping labels / `max_query_series`, not by distinct counted values. Peak sketch memory scales with group count (~16 KiB dense per group) and is not capped by `max_query_series` alone. ## Test plan - [ ] `go test ./pkg/logql/ ./pkg/logql/syntax/ ./pkg/logql/log/ ./pkg/querier/queryrange/ ./pkg/logproto/ ./pkg/chunkenc/` - [ ] Instant query returns per-group estimates; missing/empty counted fields are skipped - [ ] With `shard_aggregations: [approx_count_distinct]`, shard mapper rewrites to merge-before-estimate and merged estimates match local evaluation - [ ] Without the gate / without protobuf encoding, queries are rejected - [ ] Range queries are rejected - [ ] Staging enablement before broader rollout

signal.title: Metric queries and log queries cover different time ranges for the same request
signal.text: Log queries and histogram queries with `count_over_time` produce two different windows for the same time range and the counts don't always match. ### Steps to reproduce In our dev env, window `09:51:56.691Z` -> `09:51:57.557Z` (866ms): ``` log query {service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" -> 113 lines metric sum(count_over_time({service_name="my-service"} | detected_level="debug" [100ms])) step=100ms -> buckets at .600 .700 .800 .900 .000 .100 .200 .300 .400 .500 -> sum = 138 ``` I pulled every line in the area and checked by hand. Of those 138, **27 fall before the window start** and **2 lines inside the window are missing** because there's no bucket for them. ### Why Two things stack up. Step alignment rounds both start and end *down* to a step multiple (`queryrangebase/step_align.go:20-23`). So `.691` becomes `.600` and `.557` becomes `.500`. That alone pulls in extra data at the front and drops data off the back. Then the first bucket counts `(t - step, t]`, so it reaches back another full step behind the already-rounded start (`logql/range_vector.go:155`, `engine/internal/executor/range_aggregation.go:41-51`). Net effect, for a request of `[start, end)`: ``` actually covered: (floor(start/step)*step - step, floor(end/step)*step] ``` Up to 2 steps of extra data at the front, up to 1 step missing at the back. Log queries don't get any of this. `engine/handler.go:180-183` skips them on purpose to preserve sub-second precision, and the log splitter doesn't align either. So the two query types genuinely answer questions about different windows. ### Impact Logs Drilldown sums the volume histogram client-side and shows it next to the log line count, with no clipping (`LogsVolumePanel.tsx:146`). Users see two numbers that should match and don't. Tracked from the UI side in grafana/logs-drilldown#2049.

signal.title: Replace `go.uber.go/atomic` with Go standard library `sync/atomic`
signal.text: ## Summary We currently have a linter rule that blocks usage of `sync/atomic` and forces us to use `go.uber.go/atomic` instead. This rule was originally added because `sync/atomic` required atomic operations on primitive types, which was considered error-prone. However, since **Go 1.19**, the standard library `sync/atomic` package now includes typed wrappers (e.g., `atomic.Uint32`, `atomic.Int64`, `atomic.Bool`, etc.) that provide the same safety guarantees as `go.uber.go/atomic`. This makes the uber package redundant. ## Context Prometheus is also making this transition: - Issue: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14866 - PR: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18009 ## Proposed Changes 1. **Remove the linter rule** that blocks `sync/atomic` 2. **Migrate all `go.uber.go/atomic` usage** to the standard library `sync/atomic` typed wrappers 3. **Configure a linter rule** to block the old-style atomic functions that operate on primitive types (e.g., `atomic.AddInt64`, `atomic.LoadUint32`) to ensure we only use the new typed wrappers and avoid accidental misuse This approach gives us: - Fewer external dependencies - Alignment with the broader Go ecosystem - Same safety guarantees we had with uber/atomic ## References - Go 1.19 release notes on atomic types: https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.19#atomic_types - `sync/atomic` package docs: https://pkg.go.dev/sync/atomic

signal.title: feat: Collapse max request body size and decompressed size
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: This commit collapses the max-recv-msg-size, which measures the size of the HTTP request body, and the max decompressed size (i.e. if the request has been Gzip or Snappy compressed) into a single flag. As far as Loki is concerned, we only care about the maximum size of the actual logproto that is parsed out of the request after any decompression. It doesn't make sense to have two different flags for this with the same value. You will notice that in http.go we pass the same flag twice to push.ParseRequest. This is temporary, and the only reason for it is to make the diff smaller and easier to review. signal.title: fix(indexgateway): Cap client-side in-flight requests to avoid retry amplification
signal.text: Fixes #24051 ## What this does `poolDo` had no bound on concurrent in-flight requests to the index gateway pool. With `maxRetries = -1` (used by 6 of the 7 call sites), a client under load would serially walk every address in the pool on failure, each attempt bounded by that gateway's own admission-control queue timeout (from #23932). When every replica is shedding load, this amplifies load at exactly the moment the pool is most overloaded, instead of failing fast. ## The fix Adds a configurable client-side cap on in-flight requests (`-index-gateway-client.max-in-flight-requests`, default 2048, 0 = unlimited to match the convention used elsewhere in this file). The check runs at the very start of `poolDo`, before any tenant lookup or address resolution — once at capacity, requests are rejected immediately with a distinct error instead of retrying across the whole pool. Tracked via a new `loki_index_gateway_request_rejected_total` counter so operators can see this happening rather than it being silent. One deliberate tradeoff: the cap check is check-then-act, not a single atomic compare-and-swap, so under concurrency the actual in-flight count can briefly exceed the configured cap by a small margin. Noted in a code comment — this is acceptable for a soft limit meant to prevent amplification storms, not a hard resource cap. ## Testing Added four tests covering: rejection at cap (verified by confirming the capacity error returns before any tenant/address lookup would even be attempted), the in-flight counter decrementing after both success and failure paths (proving the `defer` fires on every exit), and `MaxInFlightRequests = 0` correctly disabling the check. Happy to adjust the default cap value or error message if you'd prefer something different.

signal.title: feat(kafka): support configurable SASL mechanism (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512)
signal.text: ## What this PR does / why we need it Loki's Kafka client hardcodes **SASL PLAIN** as the only authentication mechanism. Brokers configured with `sasl.enabled.mechanisms=SCRAM-SHA-256` or `SCRAM-SHA-512` only (e.g., AWS MSK, Confluent Cloud) immediately reject the handshake with `UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM`, making Loki impossible to use with those providers. This PR adds a new optional `kafka.sasl_mechanism` configuration parameter, allowing operators to choose between: - `PLAIN` (default, backward-compatible) - `SCRAM-SHA-256` - `SCRAM-SHA-512` ## Which issue(s) this PR fixes Fixes #21712 ## Changes ### Core Implementation - Added `SASLMechanism` field and validation constants to `pkg/kafka/config.go` - Updated `commonKafkaClientOptions` in `pkg/kafka/client/writer_client.go` to conditionally apply the configured SASL mechanism via switch statement - Vendored `github.com/twmb/franz-go/pkg/sasl/scram` sub-package (v1.20.7, already an indirect dependency) ### Tests (TDD approach) - Added `TestSASLMechanismValidation` in `pkg/kafka/config_test.go` to validate allowed mechanisms and reject invalid ones - Added `TestNewReaderClientSCRAMAuthentication` in `pkg/kafka/client/reader_client_test.go` with SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 subtests - Added `TestNewWriterClientSCRAMAuthentication` in `pkg/kafka/client/writer_client_test.go` with SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 subtests - Refactored existing reader/writer client tests to use explicit `SASLMechanism` field for clarity ### Documentation - Updated config reference in `docs/sources/shared/configuration.md` with the new `sasl_mechanism` parameter - Added upgrade note in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` explaining the new parameter, default behavior, and use cases - Added troubleshooting guidance in `docs/sources/operations/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-operations.md` for `UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM` errors ### Text Consistency - Updated flag help text in `pkg/kafka/config.go` to remove outdated "PLAIN-only" wording - Updated generated docs to match the new, mechanism-agnostic descriptions ## Special notes for your reviewer 1. **Backward Compatibility**: The default value is `PLAIN`, preserving full backward compatibility. No action is required for existing deployments. 2. **Testing**: All tests follow table-driven patterns with explicit mechanism values. signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: `Fetcher.FetchChunks` logs an object store error and then returns a nil error. The query gets fewer log lines, HTTP 200, and no signal. signal.title: fix: Recognise thanos/minio S3 throttling errors as retryable
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: S3 throttling responses (`SlowDown`, `503`, `429`) were not being treated as retryable when the object client runs on the thanos/objstore backend (`use_thanos_objstore: true`), which is the default for our object stores. `IsStorageThrottledErr` only matched the AWS SDK's `smithy.APIError`, but the thanos S3 client is backed by minio-go, which returns `minio.ErrorResponse`. As a result, on throttling: - congestion control classified the error as non-retryable, - so it never retried, and its AIMD controller never backed off, and - every throttle surfaced immediately as a `failed downloading chunks` error. This PR makes `IsStorageThrottledErr` also recognise `minio.ErrorResponse` throttling/5xx codes (with an HTTP-status fallback for 429 / any 5xx), so both the legacy AWS-SDK client and the thanos/minio client share one retryability definition. Retries and AIMD back-off now engage as designed, absorbing transient throttles instead of failing the chunk fetch. **Special notes for your reviewer**: - The fix lives in `IsStorageThrottledErr`, which is the single retryability entry point used by *both* the legacy S3 client and the thanos `ObjectClientAdapter` (`storeType == s3` → `aws.IsRetryableErr`), so both paths benefit, and there's no duplicated code-list. - `errors.As` is used so wrapped errors (thanos wraps with `pkg/errors`) are still matched. - Tests, in increasing scope: - unit: `TestIsRetryableErr` — minio `SlowDown`/`ServiceUnavailable`/`InternalError`/`TooManyRequests`, wrapped errors, status-only fallback, and negatives (`NoSuchKey`, `AccessDenied`). - wiring: `TestObjectClientAdapter_IsRetryableErr_S3Minio` — locks `storeType == s3` → minio-aware retryability. - end-to-end: `TestCongestionControl_S3Throttling_*` — drive the real AIMD controller → LimitedRetrier → thanos adapter → minio-go → fake S3 returning `503 SlowDown`, asserting retries fire, AIMD backs off, `non_retryable_errors == 0`, and a transient throttle is absorbed. - No config or API changes; behaviour only changes for previously misclassified throttling errors. **Checklist** - [ ] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory.

signal.title: feat(indexgateway): Add admission control to bound concurrent requests
signal.text: ## Summary The index gateway currently has no bound on concurrent request execution. This PR ports the admission-control pattern used in Mimir's store-gateway (same dskit building blocks): at most N requests execute at once; excess requests wait for a free slot; requests that wait longer than the configured timeout are rejected with HTTP 503. This feature is **experimental** and **disabled by default** (`-index-gateway.max-concurrent=0`). ## Error handling choice Load-shed rejections now use `httpgrpc.Error(503, ...)`, matching distributor convention (`pkg/distributor/distributor.go`). This gives us the behavior we want without broad shared-mapping changes: - No `pkg/util/server/error.go` mapping changes required. - 503 survives wrapped errors (important for `GetShards`, which wraps RPC errors). - Unrelated transport-level gRPC `Unavailable` failures are not implicitly remapped. ## Test updates Time-dependent gate tests now run under `testing/synctest`, which removes wall-clock sleeps/timeouts and makes the cancellation ordering deterministic. ## Follow-up When all replicas are saturated, retrying across replicas can amplify pressure by serially spending queue timeout at each target. Follow-up issue: https://github.com/grafana/loki/issues/24051 ## Dev validation note Cloud dev-environment validation is planned next using an in-progress harness; this PR does not include local docker-compose evidence.

signal.title: fix(operator): Specify different certs to be used by the passthrough gateway tenancy
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: Currently, you can specify custom tls for tenants, but passthrough-gateway will always disregard that setting and use default auto-generated secrets. There may be a case where you want to "Bring-Your-Own" cert, such that you don't have to use the server identity generated by default, so added a fix such that passthrough gateway uses the certs defined for `tenants.gateway.tls` ``` tenants: mode: passthrough passthrough: ca: ... gateway: tls: <-- fix: passthrough gateway now can use the tls config defined here ca: ... certificate: ... privateKey: ... ``` Adds test case based off of existing `TestBuildGateway_WithHTTPEncryption_WithCustomTLS` to validate custom cert is used by passthrough gateway Note: A volume is created for `tenants.gateway.tls.ca` but it is never used for passthrough so it is not included in the list of volumemounts.
