signal.title: chore: Read series records through one scan per postings pass
signal.text: The stream reader built a fresh decbuf for every series record: a pooled file handle, a 4 KiB bufio buffer, a seek to the record, and a read. A series ref is the record's file offset divided by 16 and postings hand out refs in ascending order, so consecutive series in a result set are usually adjacent in the file and often inside the same 4 KiB window. The read-ahead that would have covered a series' neighbours was discarded by the next ResetAt before it could be used. Hold one decbuf for the whole postings pass instead, moving forward by discarding buffered bytes when the next record is within the buffer and repositioning otherwise. Nothing depends on refs being ascending: an out-of-order ref just repositions, which costs what it costs today. This PR changes the Reader interface to support this streaming approach. Added benchmark: ``` ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼───────────────────┤ │ Benchmark │ before │ after │ Δ │ │ SeriesIteration │ 68.41 ms │ 56.36 ms │ −17.63% (p=0.002) │ ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼───────────────────┤ │ SeriesIteration B/op │ 4.320 Mi │ 2.880 Mi │ −33.32% │ ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼───────────────────┤ │ SeriesIteration allocs │ 83.44 k │ 59.91 k │ −28.20% │ ├────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼───────────────────┤ ``` Against realistic indexes with broad queries, I see improvements of 40-80%. **What this PR does / why we need it**: Part of our effort to migrate away from mmap in index gateways - we're now in the optimisation phase. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: N/A **Special notes for your reviewer**: This is best reviewed commit by commit - the first commit makes small changes in place to make a minimal diff, then the second commit refactors out a separate file. **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [x] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [x] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [x] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. signal.title: fix(storage): Pre-compute SHA-256 to avoid aws-chunked on PutObject
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: When `ChecksumAlgorithm` is set on `PutObjectInput` without a pre-computed value, the AWS SDK v2 switches to trailing-checksum mode which wraps the body in `aws-chunked` transfer encoding. OpenStack Swift and other S3-compatible backends reject this with `501 NotImplemented`. This PR pre-computes the SHA-256 hash upfront and passes it as `ChecksumSHA256`. This causes the SDK checksum middleware to detect that the header is already present and skip the `aws-chunked` trailing-checksum path entirely. This cleanly satisfies Object Lock requirements (which require the checksum header) while remaining compatible with S3-compatible backends (which don't support `aws-chunked`). **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Fixes #21791 **Special notes for your reviewer**: I've added two regression tests to `s3_storage_client_test.go`: 1. `TestPutObject_NoAWSChunkedEncoding`: Verifies that `PutObject` sends the `x-amz-checksum-sha256` as a plain header and does NOT use `Content-Encoding: aws-chunked`. 2. `TestPutObject_SwiftRejects_AWSChunked`: A mock server that behaves like OpenStack Swift (returns `501 NotImplemented` when it sees `aws-chunked`). It proves that the fix makes the request pass successfully against a Swift-like API. Because `clientutil.ReadSeeker` already guarantees the body is fully buffered in memory (`bytes.Reader`), the SHA-256 pre-computation reads from RAM and adds zero extra I/O. **Checklist** - [x] Reviewed the [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide (**required**) - [ ] Documentation added - [x] Tests updated - [x] Title matches the required conventional commits format, see [here](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) - [ ] Changes that require user attention or interaction to upgrade are documented in `docs/sources/setup/upgrade/_index.md` - [ ] If the change is deprecating or removing a configuration option, update the `deprecated-config.yaml` and `deleted-config.yaml` files respectively in the `tools/deprecated-config-checker` directory. signal.title: chore: Log usage of failed queries with failure cause
signal.text: **What this PR does / why we need it**: The query-frontend only logs query usage stats (the `metrics.go` line) for queries that execute successfully. Expensive queries that fail leave no usage record, making them invisible to usage analysis. This PR makes the query-frontend emit a dedicated log line for failed log and metric queries, reporting the number of bytes the query processed before failing and a classified, actionable cause of the failure. Implementation notes: - **The existing stats line is untouched.** The new line is emitted from the stats-collector middleware, not from `pkg/logql/metrics.go` (zero changes to that file). The successful-query stats line keeps its exact shape, is never emitted for a failed query, and failed-query usage does not feed into any of the existing usage metrics, latency histograms, or analytics. A new counter `loki_logql_querystats_failed_query_usage_recorded_total{category}` tracks the number of emitted lines. - **Scope is log/metric queries only** — the only query types whose responses carry querier-filled statistics; any other type could only ever report zeroes. - **Partial usage accumulation**: a new `stats.PartialContext` lives under its own context key so the nested stats contexts opened by the engine and the sharding middleware don't shadow it. The split and shard fan-out error paths join the stats of already-completed sub-queries into it. Sibling cancellations propagate the causal error (`context.Cause`), so a real failure isn't misreported as a client cancellation. - **Failure classification**: `server.ClassifyFailure(err)` maps an error to a bounded `failure_category` and a fine-grained `failure_reason`, reusing the canonical `ClientHTTPStatusAndError` so the logged status matches what the client is served. All configured limits classify as `failure_category=limit`. - **Sentinel-based classification for in-process errors**: byte-limit, query-length, max-entries, and parallelism rejections raised in the frontend wrap a sentinel (`errors.Is`) around the unchanged client-facing httpgrpc error. `querySizeLimiter` now carries an explicit `{limit name, sentinel, template}` spec instead of reverse-mapping its message template (`guessLimitName` is gone). Message-prefix matching remains only as documented defense-in-depth for the same limits raised on queriers or the v2 engine, where error identity cannot survive httpgrpc serialization. - `stats.Context`'s snapshot accessors now take the context mutex so snapshots no longer tear against `JoinResults`/`MergeIndex`; the failed-query path additionally avoids the residual atomic-counter race by only ever reading the `PartialContext`. - Successful shards/patterns queries no longer log a spurious "failed to record query metrics" error in the frontend. **Special notes for your reviewer**: - Client-facing error messages and status codes are unchanged throughout: the sentinel wrapping uses `%w`, and response construction extracts the embedded `httpgrpc.HTTPResponse` via `errors.As`, so the sentinel prefix never reaches the client. This invariant is pinned byte-for-byte by tests driving the real middlewares (`TestWrappedLimitErrorStatusPreserved`, plus classification assertions through `NewLimitsMiddleware`, `NewLimitedRoundTripper`, and the entries-limit tripperware). - The concurrent split fan-out path is covered by a `-race` test with live sibling writers. - The new line is emitted at info level and also covers client-cancelled queries (zero usage, `failure_category=canceled`) — expect some volume from dashboard-refresh churn; the fields make it filterable. - Failed queries that are neither split nor sharded report `total_bytes=0B` by construction: error responses carry no statistics over the wire, so only completed sibling sub-requests can contribute.

signal.title: [helm] Zone-aware ingester StatefulSets emit a duplicate `name` label and become invalid when `ingester.podLabels.name` is set
signal.text: <!-- Please keep the structure below, or your issue may be closed. --> **Describe the bug** When `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`, the three zone StatefulSet templates use the pod label `name: <prefix>ingester-zone-{a,b,c}` as the zone discriminator, and reference it from `spec.selector.matchLabels`. The same templates also append `.Values.loki.podLabels` and `.Values.ingester.podLabels` verbatim via `toYaml`, *after* their own labels and without merging. If a user sets `podLabels.name`, the rendered `spec.template.metadata.labels` therefore contains the key `name` **twice**. Two consequences: 1. The chart emits a YAML mapping with a duplicate key, which is invalid per the YAML spec regardless of what the user supplied. 2. Duplicate keys resolve last-wins, so the effective pod label becomes the user's value while `spec.selector.matchLabels` still requires the chart's. The API server rejects the StatefulSet with `` `selector` does not match template `labels` ``. The same key is also used by the per-zone headless Services (`service-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}-headless.yaml`), so a naive workaround of dropping the chart's label would leave those Services with no endpoints and break stable pod DNS. The non-zone-aware template is not affected: its selector is only `loki.ingesterSelectorLabels` and does not include `name`, so overriding `podLabels.name` there is harmless. The inconsistency looks unintentional — the zone templates added `name` to the selector without protecting it from the override path the chart itself exposes. `rollout-group` and the `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are exposed to the same collision. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0 (Loki 3.3.2). 2. Render the zone-a ingester StatefulSet with `podLabels.name` set: ```yaml # values.yaml deploymentMode: Distributed loki: storage: type: s3 bucketNames: chunks: chunks ruler: ruler admin: admin schemaConfig: configs: - from: "2024-04-01" store: tsdb object_store: s3 schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ingester: replicas: 3 podLabels: name: my-ingester # any value collides zoneAwareReplication: enabled: true read: replicas: 0 write: replicas: 0 backend: replicas: 0 ``` ``` helm template loki grafana/loki --version 6.25.0 -f values.yaml \ -s templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-a.yaml ``` 3. Apply the rendered manifest to a cluster. **Expected behavior** The chart should never emit a mapping with a duplicate key, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` should always be a subset of `spec.template.metadata.labels` for any user-supplied `podLabels`. Either the chart's structurally significant labels should win over user-supplied `podLabels`, or the chart should reject the conflicting configuration with a clear message. **Environment:** - Infrastructure: Kubernetes 1.34 (EKS), also reproducible with `helm template` alone - Deployment tool: helm (chart `grafana/loki` 6.25.0, Loki 3.3.2) **Screenshots, Alloy config, or terminal output** Rendered output, `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true` — note `name` appears twice in `template.metadata.labels`, and the selector requires the first value: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a # <-- selector requires this rollout-group: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: ingester-zone-a # <-- chart's label rollout-group: ingester name: my-ingester # <-- duplicate key, wins ``` The per-zone headless Service selects on the same key: ```yaml # service-ingester-zone-a-headless.yaml selector: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester name: ingester-zone-a rollout-group: ingester ``` Same values with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=false` — single `name`, and the selector does not reference it, so nothing breaks: ```yaml selector: matchLabels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester template: metadata: labels: app.kubernetes.io/name: loki app.kubernetes.io/instance: loki app.kubernetes.io/component: ingester app.kubernetes.io/part-of: memberlist name: my-ingester ``` `kubectl apply` of the zone-aware manifest fails with: ``` The StatefulSet "loki-ingester-zone-a" is invalid: spec.template.metadata.labels: Invalid value: map[string]string{"app.kubernetes.io/component":"ingester", "app.kubernetes.io/instance":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/name":"loki", "app.kubernetes.io/part-of":"memberlist", "name":"my-ingester", "rollout-group":"ingester"}: `selector` does not match template `labels` ``` --- ## Proposed fix `spec.selector` is immutable on a StatefulSet, so changing the discriminator to a dedicated key (e.g. `zone: zone-a`) would force existing zone-aware deployments to recreate their ingester StatefulSets. The options below keep the selector as it is. **Option 1 — merge the label sets so each key is emitted once (preferred).** In `templates/ingester/statefulset-ingester-zone-{a,b,c}.yaml`, replace the `labels:` block under `spec.template.metadata` with a single merged dict, chart labels taking precedence (sprig `merge` gives precedence to the destination): ```gotemplate labels: {{- $zoneLabels := dict "app.kubernetes.io/part-of" "memberlist" "name" (printf "%singester-zone-a" (include "loki.prefixIngesterName" .)) "rollout-group" (printf "%singester" (include "loki.prefixRolloutGroup" .)) }} {{- $userLabels := merge (deepCopy (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict)) (.Values.loki.podLabels | default dict) }} {{- toYaml (merge $zoneLabels $userLabels (fromYaml (include "loki.ingesterSelectorLabels" .))) | nindent 8 }} ``` This emits every key once and guarantees `selector ⊆ labels` for any `podLabels`. Users keep the ability to add their own labels; they simply cannot silently break the selector. **Option 2 — minimal reordering.** Move the two `podLabels` blocks *above* the chart's `name` and `rollout-group` lines, so the chart's values are emitted last and win. This fixes the selector mismatch with a three-line diff, but still emits a duplicate key, so it only addresses the second consequence. **Option 3 — fail fast (complementary to either of the above).** Reject the conflicting configuration explicitly rather than rendering something that the API server will refuse: ```gotemplate {{- if and .Values.ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled (hasKey (.Values.ingester.podLabels | default dict) "name") }} {{- fail "ingester.podLabels may not set 'name' when ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled is true: that label is the zone discriminator used by the StatefulSet selector and the per-zone headless Services" }} {{- end }} ``` Whichever option is taken, documenting `name`, `rollout-group` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` as reserved keys under `ingester.podLabels` in `values.yaml` would help. **Workaround for anyone hitting this now** Do not set `ingester.podLabels.name` with `zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true`. If the label is required (for example a metrics pipeline that relabels from the pod label `name`), the selector and the three per-zone headless Services have to be post-processed consistently onto a different discriminator key — all four objects must agree, or the Services lose their endpoints and stable pod DNS breaks.

signal.title: fix(ruler): Restore remote-write secrets lost by config Clone
signal.text: ## Summary - `RemoteWriteConfig.Clone` now restores every `Secret`-typed field reachable from a remote-write client after its YAML round-trip: - `OAuth2.ClientSecret`/`ClientCertificateKey` - `Authorization.Credentials` (including a bare `bearer_token` migrated into it during that same round-trip) - `SigV4Config.SecretKey` - `AzureADConfig.OAuth.ClientSecret`/`Certificate.CertificatePassword` - `TLSConfig.Key` at both the top level and inside `OAuth2` - `HTTPClientConfig.ProxyConnectHeader` and `OAuth2`'s own copy - `HTTPHeaders.Headers[*].Secrets` - `BasicAuth.Password` (existing) - `ProxyConnectHeader` is deep-copied via a new `cloneProxyHeader` helper so when `getTenantRemoteWriteConfig` later merges per-tenant overrides with `mergo.Merge`, reassigned maps are not aliased to the shared base config and mutated - Adds `TestTenantRemoteWriteOAuth2SecretSurvivesClone`, reproducing the leak through the real `getTenantConfig` path rather than calling `Clone` directly. - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_RestoresSecrets`, which reflects over `RemoteWriteConfig`'s type graph to find every reachable `Secret` field, asserts a fixture sets a value at each one, then asserts `Clone` preserves every one of them. - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_DoesNotAliasContainers`, asserting that mutating a clone's map- or slice-typed secret containers doesn't affect the original - Adds `TestRemoteWriteConfigClone_RestoresMigratedBearerToken`, covering the `bearer_token` case separately since the field its secret ends up in differs from the field it started in. `Clone` round-trips a `RemoteWriteConfig` through YAML to produce an independent per-tenant copy, but Prometheus's `config_util.Secret` type obfuscates several values to the literal string `<secret>`. Before this change `Clone` only restored `BasicAuth.Password`, so every other auth mechanism silently lost its real secret the moment a tenant's config was cloned The comprehensive test walks the type graph with reflection rather than checking a fixed field list, so a future Prometheus vendor bump that adds a new `Secret` field anywhere in this type graph fails the coverage check immediately

signal.title: docs: Note that index/stats and index/volume are not deletion-aware
signal.text: Documents the caveat reported in #23807. `SelectLogs` and `SelectSamples` pass the filters from pending and recently processed delete requests into the query via `deletion.DeletesForUserQuery` (`pkg/querier/querier.go`), so log and metric queries are exact as soon as a delete request is processed. `IndexStats` and `Volume` in the same file take no delete parameters — they report what the index holds, so the same stream selector can keep reporting deleted data until the compactor has rewritten the index and the pre-rewrite index files have aged out. `Volume` also fans out to the ingesters, whose not-yet-flushed chunks are counted before any delete filtering applies to them, while `IndexStats` is store-only. The reference already carries a caveats list for `index/stats`; this adds the deletion caveat there and an equivalent note on `index/volume` / `index/volume_range`, which had none. It also points at `bytes_over_time` for accounting that has to be exact, since that path is deletion-aware. This is documentation only. The reporter's second ask — making these endpoints deletion-aware, or deduplicating chunk identity across the merged compactor-rewritten and ingester-uploaded index views — is a behaviour change I did not want to guess at, so I have left it to #23807. Verified against `main`: the delete-parameter asymmetry between `SelectLogs`/`SelectSamples` and `IndexStats`/`Volume` is still present, and `Volume` still queries the ingesters.

signal.title: feat(storage): Add OCI Thanos object store backend
signal.text: ## Problem Loki does not currently expose OCI Object Storage as a supported Thanos object-store backend. OCI users therefore have to use the S3-compatible API and static Customer Secret Keys. This prevents using OCI-native authentication mechanisms such as: - OKE Workload Identity - Instance Principal ## Proposed solution Add `oci` to Loki's Thanos object-store backends by reusing the OCI provider from Thanos objstore. Proposed configuration: ``` storage_config: use_thanos_objstore: true object_store: oci: provider: instance-principal bucket: loki-data region: ap-tokyo-1 max_request_retries: 3 request_retry_interval: 1 schema_config: configs: - from: 2026-08-01 store: tsdb object_store: oci schema: v13 index: prefix: index_ period: 24h ``` ## Security benefit No OCI Customer Secret Key needs to be stored in Loki configuration or Kubernetes Secrets. ## Scope - Loki TSDB object storage - Instance Principal - Unit tests - OCI/OKE integration test documentation Named stores and Helm chart support can be submitted separately. ## Validation A standalone Thanos OCI client has already been validated successfully against OCI Object Storage from OKE using Instance Principal. Fixes #23687
